topic.angle: The gold foil experiment and the nucleus

panels.text: Manchester, 1909. In Ernest Rutherford's lab, Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden fire alpha particles from radium at a very thin gold foil and count flashes on a screen.
The popular atom model predicted that the particles should all go almost straight through.
But about 1 in 8000 bounced back. Rutherford said it was as unlikely as a huge shell fired at tissue paper coming back to hit you.
His explanation: an atom has a tiny, dense centre holding most of its mass. Most particles sail past it through the empty space around it, and rare near-hits scatter them.

probes.question: What did the rare bounced-back particles show about atoms?
options: Atoms are solid balls all the way through
A tiny central nucleus holds most of the atom's mass, with empty space around it
Electrons are heavier than the nucleus

probes.question: True or false: Geiger and Marsden's experiment used a very thin gold foil.

claims.claim: Geiger and Marsden worked under Rutherford at the University of Manchester, 1909
claims.quote: The experiments were performed between 1906 and 1913 by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden under the direction of Ernest Rutherford at the Physical Laboratories of the University of Manchester .

claims.claim: In 1909 they found foils could scatter some alpha particles in all directions
claims.quote: In a 1909 experiment, Geiger and Marsden discovered that the metal foils could scatter some alpha particles in all directions

claims.claim: They counted flashes of light on a screen
claims.quote: Each impact of an alpha particle on the screen produced a tiny flash of light.

claims.claim: They used a very thin gold foil (probe 2)
claims.quote: they tested a variety of metals, but favoured gold because they could make the foil very thin, as gold is the most malleable metal.
As a source of alpha particles, Rutherford's substance of choice was radium

claims.claim: The popular model predicted particles should pass almost straight through
claims.quote: Had Thomson's model been correct, all the alpha particles should have passed through the foil with minimal scattering.
They were able to demonstrate that 1 in 8000 alpha particle collisions were diffuse reflections.

claims.claim: Rutherford compared it to a huge shell fired at tissue paper coming back
claims.quote: It was almost as incredible as if you fired a 15-inch shell at a piece of tissue paper and it came back and hit you.

claims.claim: Tiny dense centre holding most of the atom's mass (probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: The mass of heavy atoms such as gold is mostly concentrated in the central charge region

claims.claim: Most particles pass through empty space; rare close encounters scatter them
claims.quote: reflecting the tiny nucleus surrounded by empty space.
